result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals. While the infrastructure includes sidewalks and a small median refuge, the multi-lane configuration creates a long crossing distance and high exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to multiple lanes of traffic for an extended period.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Multi-lane Threat
hazards.description: Multiple travel lanes in the same direction can lead to situations where one vehicle stops for a pedestrian but obscures them from drivers in adjacent lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes approaching the crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicle traffic receives a green light.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Refuge
interventions.description: Expand the existing median refuge into a larger, more protective island with physical barriers.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and wide, well-maintained sidewalks. However, the large corner radius and lack of physical protection at the curb may encourage higher vehicle turning speeds, increasing risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Large corner radius
hazards.description: The wide curb radius at the intersection allows vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, increasing the risk of collisions with pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection
hazards.description: There is no physical barrier or bollard system to protect pedestrians waiting at the corner from vehicles overshooting the turn.

interventions.title: Curb Extension (Bulbout)
interventions.description: Install a curb extension to reduce the turning radius for vehicles and shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban multi-lane roadway with a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the long crossing distance and lack of a median refuge increase exposure to vehicle traffic in a high-density commercial area.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, significantly increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk spanning the entire width of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked along the curb near the intersection may block sightlines between pedestrians entering the crosswalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway immediately preceding the crosswalk

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and traffic signals. Active construction on the far side of the street introduces barriers and potential sidewalk obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Construction Obstruction
hazards.description: Blue construction fencing and concrete barriers appear to block the sidewalk path on the far side of the intersection.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large truck is parked near the intersection, which may block the view between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Detour Signage
interventions.description: Provide clear signage and a safe, accessible temporary path around the construction site to maintain pedestrian connectivity.
